transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. It's nice to meet you too. Well, I'm here because I keep getting these awful doubts that I've missed something important. 

It could be a number on the mortgage payment, a clause in a client proof for work, or even just a door not being latched. And the thing is, even when I know I already checked it, the thought just barges right back in. It's always something like, "What if this is the mistake that costs you everything?" It's just getting to be too much to deal with on my own.
When that doubt hits, do you find yourself checking the thing over and over?

Yes, I do. I end up reopening files, or... rereading emails I just sent. I'll go back and check the online payment confirmation again and again. Sometimes I even just say the figures silently in my head until they finally feel, I don't know, settled. It's really impacting my work, honestly, because it can turn a simple invoice or just a minor logo revision into hours of time that I just can't bill for.
When these thoughts come up, do they feel intrusive and unwanted to you?

Yes, absolutely. Like I mentioned a minute ago, they really just barge right in. I definitely don't want them there. I'll know I already checked a client proof or the mortgage payment, but that awful doubt that I've missed something important just forces its way into my head anyway. It's very intrusive. Having that "what if this is the mistake that costs you everything" thought constantly popping up is completely unwanted.
When you go back and check, is it mainly to relieve the anxiety from the doubt?

Yes, exactly. The checking is really just to make that awful anxious feeling go away. 

Like I was saying before, I end up reopening files, rereading emails, or checking those online payment confirmations again and again. Or I'll repeat the numbers silently in my head... I just keep doing it until things finally feel, well, "settled," and the panic drops. But chasing that relief is exactly what turns a simple invoice or a minor logo revision into hours of time that I just can't bill for.
Do you feel that the amount of checking you do is excessive?

Yes, I really do. I mean, like I've been saying, spending hours on a simple invoice or a minor logo revision is just... it's way too much. Reopening the same files, going over those emails and payment confirmations, doing the numbers in my head over and over until I feel settled—it's completely out of proportion to the actual task. So, yes, I know it's extremely excessive.
Do these checking habits feel like they fit with the kind of person you naturally are?

No, they really don't. I've always been a careful person—you have to be in graphic design, you know, paying attention to details—but this is different. It doesn't feel like me at all. I've always prided myself on being efficient and getting things done. So being stuck in this loop of checking and re-checking... it just feels like something else has taken over. It's not who I am.
Do you feel that these doubts and the checking they lead to are unreasonable?

Yes, absolutely. I know it's completely unreasonable. Logically, I know that checking a payment confirmation once is enough, and looking at it ten more times isn't going to change anything. Or that a logo file doesn't just magically alter itself after I've saved it. But even knowing how irrational it is doesn't stop the feeling that I have to do it. It's incredibly frustrating because my brain knows it makes no sense, but I still can't seem to stop.
